newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia proceeding with Petronas-Iran deal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia proceeding with Petronas-Iran deal.

text.p: Malaysia intends to proceed with a deal for national oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd to buy a stake in two Iranian oil fields despite the threat of U.S. sanctions against the company, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday.
"We will go on (with the deal)," he told reporters at a function for state utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd. "We are a sovereign nation. We will not submit to what the U.S. dictates to us."
Petronas has a 30 percent stake in Iran's Sirri oilfields exploration project, which also involves French company Total SA.
On Tuesday, an aide to U.S. Senator Alfonso D'Amato said the U.S. may consider taking action against Petronas over the stake.
The investment in the $600 million project puts Petronas over the $40 million a year level that the U.S. has said non-U.S. firms can invest in Iran and Libya's oil and gas sectors.
Rumours about imminent sanctions against Petronas contributed to a sharp drop in the ringgit on Wednesday.

Mahathir remained adamant about not bowing to the U.S. threats. "We will not submit to what the U.S. dictates to us," he told reporters on Thursday. "We have struggled to become a nation. We will not be colonised again."
